subject: zoology_2
question_text: How is sex determined in human beings?

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.38, SAQ 32. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05 after the examiner audit: the two common-mistake entries no longer call the all-chromosome notations 46,XX and 23,X errors, because both are correct ways of writing the same karyotype.

steps.label: The XX-XY mechanism
steps.why: Only one of the 23 pairs differs between the sexes, so that single pair carries the whole decision.
common_mistakes: Saying all 23 pairs differ. Only one pair does.
steps.memory_tip: 22 pairs the same, one pair different.
steps.margin_note: Name the type, then the numbers.
lines: The sex determining mechanism in humans is
Of the 23 pairs of chromosomes, 22 pairs
are exactly the same in both males and

steps.label: The two karyotypes
steps.why: Writing the karyotype as 44 plus the sex pair makes clear that only the last pair differs.
common_mistakes: Mixing the two notations in one answer. Write 44XX, which means 44 autosomes plus XX. The notation 46,XX counts all 46 chromosomes and means the same thing.
steps.margin_note: Write both karyotypes on one line each.

steps.label: The gametes
steps.why: The mother can only ever give an X, so she cannot influence the sex of the child at all.
common_mistakes: Giving the female two kinds of gamete. She makes one kind.
Dropping the autosomes and writing only X. Write 22X, which means 22 autosomes plus one X. The notation 23,X counts all 23 chromosomes of the gamete and means the same thing.
steps.memory_tip: Ova are all 22X; sperm are 22X or 22Y.

gametes. The male produces two types.
Gametes produced by the female are 22X.

steps.label: Which sperm gives which child
steps.why: Since the two kinds of sperm are made in equal numbers, each pregnancy has the same chance either way.
common_mistakes: Blaming the mother for the sex of the child.
steps.memory_tip: The sperm decides, and it is fifty-fifty every time.

lines.text: Each pregnancy is a 50 percent chance either way

insider_note: End with the 50 percent line. It answers the question behind the question and is a marked point in its own right.
